Overview for the managers' team

Transport Planner

What the Route Planner does today, and what it can become: one place for the department's daily operations

Route Planner v0.12.6 BETAOne HTML file, no serverChrome or EdgeWorks from the shared folder

All screens in this deck are from the demo week. The data is invented; no customer or staff data is shown.

Why it exists

One tool to plan, record and print each day's deliveries

Plan

Load the day's planning and RESOURCES files, see drops by bay on a map, move, defer, split or insert orders.

Record

Every planning change is logged with who made it and when, ready to update the other systems.

Collect

Uplifts outstanding are matched with the day's deliveries, confirmed by the planner and tracked until charged.

Print

Check sheets and uplift dockets organised by route, in the order of the plan.

Control

Four roles, one laptop per person, access checked before the planner opens.

Daily flow

How a planning day works

1. Pick your name→ 2. Home→ 3. Load the day's reports→ 4. Planning & uplifts→ 5. Change report→ 6. Save→ 7. Printing

Master

Everything, incl. users, bay colours and the Delivery Shortages link.

Manager

Plans and undoes; cannot manage users.

User

Plans the day, confirms uplifts and saves.

Viewer

Read-only; can print and export.
Built

Safe start and reports

  • The planner is locked until a name is picked and the laptop, folder and files pass the checks.
  • What are you planning? Load a saved plan, or start a New Plan and pick the day on Home.
  • 📁 Reports: Master Data, Planning Data by week and Saved Plans, each file marked loaded, changed or not loaded.
  • Reports uploaded from the computer are saved in their week folder with a clear name.
Built · new in v0.12

Home page

  • The planner opens on the days of the week, one row per day.
  • A planned day shows bays, drops, orders (deferred out, deferred in, reallocated, P&W), kgs, km, pallets, products (CS / EA / KEG) and uplifts planned and complete. Click it to open it in Planning.
  • A day with no plan is grey; click it to create the plan.
  • The week's totals and the uplifts outstanding sit under the title.
Built

Planning

  • Routes with driver, helper, truck, drops, kg, pallets and km.
  • Move or defer one drop or a selected group, with a reason.
  • Split a customer's orders, insert an order, add a route or a new day.
  • Tag each order's docket as P&W or Check Sheet.
  • The map follows the routes you open (it needs internet).
Built

Resources

  • The day's routes, drivers, helpers and trucks as an Excel-like sheet.
  • Weeks and days are buttons: filled days have a plan open, dashed days have none.
  • Copy and paste blocks, also to and from Excel; export in the RESOURCES layout.
  • Drops and Kgs follow the plan automatically.
Built · new in v0.12

Uplifts in Planning

  • The JDE CU report replaces the two scripts of the Uplift control workbook.
  • Each uplift outstanding is matched with the customer's deliveries, by Ship To or by the same address.
  • A match is a proposal until the planner confirms it; an uplift can also be put on any route by hand.
  • New UPLIFT column in the route list; triangles on the map.
Built · new in v0.12

Uplift Control

  • Summary: every uplift with status, value, route, day planned (Auto or Manual · user), first and last seen and the last comment.
  • Planned days: confirm the matches of a day, one by one or all at once. The day keeps its uplifts and shows completed or not done.
  • Attempts: an uplift not done is planned again as the 2nd attempt, tagged in Printing too.
  • ⓘ History of each order: report snapshots, allocations, confirmations and comments, with who and when.
  • Drop the report on the page; an order already there is updated, never duplicated. An order no longer in the report is archived with its notes.
  • Export to Excel in the workbook's Summary / Archive layout.
Built

Change report

  • Every planning change by section: deferred, reallocated, inserted, new routes, docket changes, customer details and uplifts planned.
  • Shows who made each change and when.
  • Search, filter, sort and undo; export to Excel or print with a signature line.
  • The P&W balloon filters every section to Pink & White orders.
Built

Printing

  • Delivery: the JDE check-sheet PDF is organised with one cover per route, in plan order. Moved orders go to their new route, deferred orders to their own section.
  • Uplift: the uplift docket PDF is matched with the report and organised the same way, in a PDF of its own.
  • Pages nobody can read go to REVIEW; loads not in Resources go to UNASSIGNED. Integrity checks must pass.
  • Reprint a Docket finds any order or uplift.
Built

Customers and Options

  • Customers: every customer from the master file by delivery day, area and bay; search, fix missing map locations, edit or add. Edits are logged.
  • Options: bay colours, users and roles (Master only), every file loaded with who and when, and the theme.
Built

The future · Products

Products and P&W tracking

Partly built

Products under each order

The products report is matched by order number and shown under the order in Planning. Totals per customer in CS, EA and KEG; if an order is split, its totals follow it. The list is closed by default and opens with ›.
To be supplied

Units rule

CS = cases, EA = singles, KEG = Sls Cd5 LP. Some customers order by bottle: 10 bottles in boxes of 6 should be 1 CS and 4 EA. The conversion rule is still to be supplied.
Idea

Orders lost from tracking

Planning extracts DIPS orders only. P&W dockets, EMO orders and deliveries on a date other than the scheduled pick only show up on the POD report, after the fact. The app would catch them and show them to the planner.
The future · Manifest and POD

Reports that are already up to date

Idea

Manifest

  • Printed from the app's records, so it already includes the day's rework.
  • Can carry the extra information the department needs.
  • Used well, the manifest itself can be redesigned for a new process.
Idea

POD report

  • The app already knows each order's route, moves and deferrals.
  • The report is generated with those statuses filled in.
  • Investigations are faster and more accurate.

Today POD reports are listed in the Reports window but cannot be imported yet.

The future · What it needs

From prototype to a department tool

Today

One HTML file. Plans and records live in files on the shared drive and in each browser. Roles are guardrails in the browser.

Why that matters

Time sheets, crew data and an audit trail need one shared copy, real sign-in and records that can't be overwritten.

The path

A server with company sign-in (Microsoft Entra ID), one shared plan per day, reports read automatically and an append-only log. The steps are written in the backend blueprint.

The prototype stays useful on that path: its demo and full-feature test become the acceptance test for the production version.

For discussion

What should the application be called?

It is Route Planner today. Once crew, vehicles and time sheets are in, it does more than plan routes.

Current proposal

Transport Planner

Clear and already the project's name.
Option

Transport Hub

Says it is the one place for the department.
Option

Dispatch Desk

Short; names the daily job of sending loads out.
Option

TOPS

Transport Operations Planning System; works as a short name in conversation.
